doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Learning from experience: warm-up bands and jamming versus schools
summary: Discussion of how road experience and jam sessions taught musicians what school cannot.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I want to ask you, I want to follow in on that and ask for some comparisons there. Because this music is experiential.
Yes you have to have something to play about.

And I want you to talk about that. Because then I’m going to ask you a little later about some questions about some of the marvelous big bands that you played with. But at that time you had the university of Basie. The university of Ellington.
Well but that’s the tops. You don’t start out at the top you know.
Well take us to prep school then.

Well you just do something, you know it’s like anything else you do, the more you live, the more experience you get and the more you know what’s going on hopefully. And that’s what that stuff was all about. They weren’t good bands, but they were bands. And I really feel sorry for the young people now as far as that goes. Because there is no warm- © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
up place like that. There’s no place to get that experience you know. And you can’t get out of high school and go straight with Count Basie’s band.
Well actually, Billy and I, we had the experience and the feeling of that, going to clubs and jamming, you know, like jazz clubs.

You know like jamming, and the guys would let you sit in if they are nice, you understand what I’m saying? But I mean you don’t find that nowadays. A kid will come out of high school or maybe the Berklee or something like that, you know. But it’s nothing like I mean in other words hearing it in the street, let’s put it that way, I mean because that’s where jazz comes from you know, from the street, you know. Because the blackboard can’t talk. But I’m not putting the schools down at all, talking about hands-on experiences. It’s just fabulous you know.
